facts: No: press back is refused on iOS by design, because iOS has no back button and an edge swipe is a different event an app can tell apart.
The refusal names the alternatives: tap the navigation bar's back button, or ask for the swipe by name with press back --gesture (app_press with gesture true).
On iOS --gesture swipes in from the left edge starting in the navigation bar, because a list row with swipe actions takes a swipe started on it.
note: BACK.md#ios says it is refused but not what to do in Mobium; that is in BACK.md 'In Mobium' (fixed 2026-10-01, back.sh) and the skill, both of which retrieval ranked first and second, so ADD both. Checked against internal/mobiumdriver/buttons.go:233-240 and schema.go:1409-1415. The stored answer, 'use press back --gesture', is right; the draft facts missed the gesture.

findings.what: The iOS section's table says press back is 'refused, with the reason' and never mentions press back --gesture, which since 2026-10-01 is Mobium's swipe back on iOS; a reader of that section alone, or a retriever, gets no way back. One line pointing at --gesture would close it.
findings.evidence: docs/BACK.md:193-195 '`press back --gesture` (`app_press` with `gesture`) swipes in from the left edge, mid-height on Android and in the navigation bar on iOS'
